title: External research as product canon
canonical_summary: Make the external research capability a single owner: the five research stages and their admitted inputs with the decision-leakage boundary, the four finding classes and the adjudicated union, delivery of capability and product-choice findings as DL-036 packets, the correction landing path, the wait for the user's answer, budget accounting and the four user-set limits, review configuration and the optional breadth stage, the per-topic latency target, adjudication truthfulness, and run provenance.
gui_classification_reason: Process, accounting and provenance semantics; the user-visible research surfaces are specified in their UI owners, so this atom is not GUI work.
negative_constraints: Do not let a research finding approve, verify, complete, schedule or land anything.
Do not admit a decision record, answered packet or decision sheet into any research stage.
Do not promise a stage, bound or figure the September 2026 campaign did not exercise.
Do not quote a turn-capped arm's recall as a model result or generalize one frozen case into a ranking.

title: External research static contract family
canonical_summary: Six closed record shapes for the research job, the classified finding, the decision packet, the decision card, the budget receipt and the run manifest, with 12 positive and 30 negative fixtures in which each negative mutates one named positive and names the single constraint it must fail, registered in the closed contracts pack list.
gui_classification_reason: The decision packet and card records carry user-visible chat content, so the family includes a GUI obligation.
negative_constraints: Do not infer runtime, provider, recovery, security, visual or performance results from fixture validation.
Do not add schemas or fixture pairs to the gate through an ambient glob.
Do not change any behaviour of the contracts verifier beyond registering this pair.

title: Research packets reuse the DL-036 decision flow unchanged
canonical_summary: Assistant Chat presents research packets through the artifact and one-at-a-time card flow it already owns, with the fixed four-response set and text status labels; External Research supplies the packet content and the finding behind each item, and a correction-class finding never becomes a card.
gui_classification_reason: The artifact, the cards and their responses are user-visible chat surfaces.
negative_constraints: Do not add, remove or reorder a response for research packets.
Do not present a correction-class finding as a decision card.
Do not introduce colored border bars, stripes or emoji glyphs.

title: A research wave lands through a registered ledger
canonical_summary: A research wave that changes canon lands through a registered v2 ledger carrying its corrections, atoms, decisions, answered questions and compile queue; research bundles are cited by path and SHA-256 rather than copied in; and the ledger records the landing without authorizing it.
gui_classification_reason: Ledger landing boundaries are planning-governance behavior, not GUI work.
negative_constraints: Do not treat a ledger record as the authorization for a canon change.
Do not copy a research bundle into the ledger as canonical prose.
Do not leave a research wave's open question as a placeholder in canon.

title: Settings holds the four research limit values
canonical_summary: The per-topic cost cap, the per-job response and time limits, the lifetime cap per arm and the unresolved-usage disposition are Project-scoped Settings values held by the Settings owner and its inventory, while their meaning and defaults belong to External Research; the inventory rows are added in the authorized inventory wave and none is claimed to exist yet.
gui_classification_reason: The four limits are user-visible Settings controls with explanatory copy.
negative_constraints: Do not store a research limit value outside the Settings owner and its inventory.
Do not hide retained unresolved usage under either disposition.
Do not claim an inventory row that has not been added.
